title: cairn/tools/base publishes cairn_test_argv, a bash-free cairn test entry on Windows
intention: cairn_test_argv(*args) -> (argv, env, cwd), beside bash_script_argv: on POSIX [bin/cairn, test, *args] unchanged; on Windows [sys.executable, -m, cairn.devices.tester.cli, *args] with cwd REPO, CAIRN_TESTER_CALLER_CWD the caller's cwd and PYTHONUTF8=1, so no bash starts.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on akienyoga9i: bin/cmd/test is a bash shim holding no logic (cd REPO; CAIRN_TESTER_CALLER_CWD=$PWD; exec python -m cairn.devices.tester.cli), and MSYS bash cannot start at Low integrity (56b61c10bdbe D8), so every proof that runs bin/cairn test on Windows is a detect-kind run. A plain tool (outline 2.3.7.1: no fifth published client tool) gives every component's proofs one bash-free entry; it starts the tester's public CLI as a process and imports nothing from the tester.
traces_to: Law 4, RULE 1 (the tester's CLI is its public interface; a tool has users, not an owner).
how: D1 cairn_test_argv in script_argv.py beside bash_script_argv; D2 a red-first proof in base's proofs. Hollow: remove the function.
